editorial.headline: Fertiliser and Pest-Control Retail: Open Nationally, Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This specialist retail activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership across every listed business scale, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks PMA registration there.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. That is the controlling local fact, despite the national record classifying the activity as TERBUKA and setting a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. The activity is specialist retail for fertilisers and pest-control products, not a broad label for agricultural commerce. Its subject is the retail sale of inputs used to nourish crops or deal with pest pressure. The scope also records direct sales, placing the activity in a sales setting as well as in a clearly defined product field.

The product range is specific enough to give the activity a distinct retail identity. It includes single manufactured fertilisers such as urea, ZA, TSP and DSP; compound and mixed fertilisers, including monoammonium phosphate, diammonium phosphate and nitrogen-phosphate-potassium products; and natural fertilisers such as compost, dolomite and lime. The pest-control side is equally broad within its speciality: insecticides, fungicides, rodenticides, herbicides, nematicides and acaricides are all named. This is a retail operation built around fertilisation and pest-management products, across manufactured, mixed and natural forms.

The national entry makes room for micro, small, medium and large businesses. That scale coverage is stated expressly, so the record does not confine the activity to a particular size of operation. Its PMA position is equally direct: TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Read nationally, those fields support one uncomplicated conclusion: foreign ownership may reach the full 100% ceiling for this retail activity.

Bali changes the operating conclusion, without changing the national ceiling. At the large scale, the OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope in the record. Bali’s permanent, island-wide rule blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The record links this result to the Bali moratorium noted in May 2026. A national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling does not overcome Bali’s permanent PMA block for this activity. For a foreign founder, the conclusion is not a qualified Bali opening: registration in Bali is blocked.
